what: A `macro_rules!` attribute rule's arguments were dropped: `attr(<args>) (<item>) => ..` kept its item pattern only (crates/mbe/src/parser.rs had a FIXME), so `#[m(anything)]` expanded as `#[m]` with no error, where the pinned nightly matches the arguments. Found because #[bstd::test(without(Crashes))] needs them.
cause: rust-analyzer's partial support was inherited with its FIXME
whys: arguments were parsed and thrown away
an unsupported shape was accepted quietly instead of refused (rule no-fallback)
no test called a declarative attr macro with arguments
class: a syntax blaze parses and then ignores: the program builds and means something else
prevention: built: the arguments are matched (mbe::MacroCall carries them; 02d84d0b43). Still open in the same class: `#[m = value]` on a declarative attr macro arrives with no arguments and is taken as `#[m]`, where rustc refuses it
